facts.statement: Apatoraptor is a genus of caenagnathid dinosaur containing only one known species, A. pennatus.
facts.quote: Apatoraptor (meaning "deceptive thief") is a genus of caenagnathid dinosaur which contains a single species, A. pennatus.

facts.statement: The species Apatoraptor pennatus was formally named and described by Gregory F. Funston and Philip John Currie in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, the type species Apatoraptor pennatus was named and described by Gregory F. Funston and Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: The specific name pennatus means "feathered" in Latin, based on quill knobs found on the ulna that indicate the animal had wings.
facts.quote: The specific name means "feathered" in Latin, referring to the find of quill knobs on the ulna, showing the animal had wings.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Apatoraptor was found in the Campanian-aged Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.
facts.quote: The only known specimen was discovered in the Campanian-aged Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta.

facts.statement: Apatoraptor is classified within the family Caenagnathidae and is considered a possible sister species to Elmisaurus.
facts.quote: Apatoraptor was, within the Oviraptorosauria, placed in the Caenagnathidae, in a derived position as a possible sister species of Elmisaurus.

facts.statement: A theropod skeleton was discovered in 1993 at Drumheller, Alberta, three kilometers west of the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology.
facts.quote: In 1993, at Drumheller in Alberta, three kilometres west of the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology, a skeleton was found of a theropod.

facts.statement: Research on the fossil resumed in 2008, leading to the discovery that it represented a species previously unknown to science.
facts.quote: In 2008, research was resumed, and only then was it discovered that the fossil represented a species new to science.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, TMP 1993.051.0001, was found in the Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation from the Campanian period.
facts.quote: The holotype TMP 1993.051.0001 was found in a layer of the Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation dating from the Campanian.

facts.statement: The fossil consists of a largely articulated partial skeleton that includes a skull.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton with skull. The fossil was largely found articulated.

facts.statement: The fossil includes a palatine bone, lower jaws, hyoid, vertebrae, ribs, shoulder girdle, arm, sternum, belly ribs, and right leg bones.
facts.quote: It contains a palatine bone, the lower jaws, a hyoid, a complete series of neck and back vertebrae, ribs, the right shoulder girdle, the right arm, a sternum, belly ribs, a right ilium, a right thighbone, a right shinbone and a right calfbone.

facts.statement: The fossil was further investigated using a CAT-scan.
facts.quote: It was further investigated by means of a CAT-scan.

facts.statement: Apatoraptor is placed within the Oviraptorosauria group, specifically in the family Caenagnathidae, as a possible sister taxon to Elmisaurus.
facts.quote: Apatoraptor fue situado dentro del grupo de los Oviraptorosauria, específicamente en la familia Caenagnathidae, en una posición avanzada como el posible taxón hermano de Elmisaurus.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Apatoraptor as the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Apatoraptor lived approximately 74 million years ago during the Campanian stage in what is now North America.
rejected.quote: Apatoraptor pennatus... vivió hace 74 millones de años durante el Campaniense en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.
